Girl dinner
GURL DIN-er
noun phrase (Gen-Z slang)
Coined in a May 2023 TikTok by Olivia Maher, who showed a plate of bread, cheese, grapes, and pickles and called it "girl dinner"; the clip went viral and the phrase became a summer-2023 trend of snack-plate meals assembled without cooking. Spin-offs followed ("boy dinner," "girl lunch"). Some commentators noted the trend could mask under-eating; most users meant it as a joke about low-effort meals.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a girl dinner is a plate of odds and ends — cheese, crackers, fruit, a pickle — eaten instead of a cooked meal, usually alone, usually filmed. It is a joke about how little effort a person will make for herself. The Christian observation: Scripture has no quarrel with a simple meal. "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith" (Pro 15:17); the plainest plate is a feast if it is eaten with joy and thanks (Ecc 9:7). What the Bible does notice is the table. The first church "did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart," breaking bread "from house to house" (Act 2:46): meals in Scripture are shared, and the shared table is where love is shown. The woman of Proverbs 31 "riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household" (Pro 31:15) — her table feeds others. A girl dinner eaten alone in front of a phone is harmless once; as a way of life it is a quiet loneliness. And a parent should watch the shadow side the trend sometimes hides: a daughter who is not eating. A father tells his daughter: eat your simple plate with joy and thanks, and come sit with us; whether we eat or drink, we do it to the glory of God (1Co 10:31) — together, at a table.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (TikTok, May 2023) for a snack-plate meal assembled without cooking — a harmless joke Scripture welcomes with thanks, while calling meals back to the shared table.

expand to see more

GIRL DINNER, n. phr. (Gen-Z slang, 2023–present; TikTok) A meal made of snacks and leftovers — cheese, crackers, fruit, pickles — eaten without cooking. "Tonight’s girl dinner: popcorn and grapes."

Spin-offs: boy dinner, girl lunch, girl breakfast.

Sometimes criticized as making under-eating look cute.

Webster (1828), root word dinner: “DINNER, noun [&hellip;] 1. The meal taken about the middle of the day; or the principal meal of the day, eaten between noon and evening. 2. An entertainment; a feast. Behold, I have prepared my dinner Matthew 22:4.”

Decode for parents: usually a joke about a lazy meal. Notice if it is every meal, and if it is always alone.

Key Scripture

Pro 15:17 — "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith."

Ecc 9:7 — "Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works."

Act 2:46 — "And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart,"

Pro 31:15 — "She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens."

1Co 10:31 — "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God."

Modern Corruption

Girl dinner is a light joke about a simple meal; its drift is the solitary plate filmed for strangers in place of the shared table, and sometimes a cover for not eating at all.

expand to see more

A plate of cheese and grapes is not a sin; Proverbs prefers a dinner of herbs with love to a banquet with hatred (Pro 15:17). The drift is subtler. The trend celebrates eating alone, eating for the camera, and eating as an afterthought, in a generation that already eats most meals by itself. Scripture’s meals are communal: Passover by households, the church breaking bread from house to house (Act 2:46), the Lord’s Supper at one table.

There is also a shadow a parent should not miss. A trend that makes a near-empty plate look charming can give cover to a daughter who is restricting food. Ask gently, watch kindly, and set a table she wants to come to. Eat simply, eat with joy (Ecc 9:7), eat together, and do it to the glory of God (1Co 10:31).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Girl + dinner → May 2023 viral TikTok (Olivia Maher) → summer-2023 snack-plate trend → general joke for a low-effort meal.

expand to see more

Middle English gurle — a child, later a young woman

Old French disner — to dine; English dinner, the main meal

May 2023: viral TikTok of a snack plate called "girl dinner"

Summer 2023: trend, spin-offs (boy dinner), think-pieces

Now a general joke for an uncooked meal

Usage

""Mom’s out so it’s girl dinner: crackers and a cheese stick.""

"Better a dinner of herbs where love is (Pro 15:17) — and better at a table than alone."

"Whether ye eat or drink, do all to the glory of God (1Co 10:31)."
